builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FPGAFly: A 166.7k-Neuron Fruit-Fly Connectome on One FPGA via Deferred Spike Expansion and Shared-Codeword States
summary: The method replaces per-synapse spike expansion and 41-bit per-neuron state storage with one 64-bit descriptor per spike expanded later in source-ID order, plus a 24-bit state encoding that shares codewords across normal, refractory, and out-of-range states. The cost is additional decoding logic (1245 LUTs), quantization of out-of-range states, and a hard dependency on a specific FPGA target (Gowin GW5AST-LV138) with custom RTL design. It can fail if connectivity or state precision exceeds the encoding's assumptions, if non-LIF neuron dynamics are needed, or if the design must be ported to different hardware, since the gains are tied to that device's BSRAM and LUT budget.
rationale: This is FPGA-based neuromorphic simulation of an insect connectome, unrelated to LLM training, inference, or agent systems, so it offers no actionable technique for the reader's production constraints.
technique: Deferred spike expansion and shared-codeword neuron states on FPGA

claims.statement: The method replaces per-synapse spike expansion and 41-bit per-neuron state storage with one 64-bit descriptor per spike expanded later in source-ID order, plus a 24-bit state encoding that shares codewords across normal, refractory, and out-of-range states. The cost is additional decoding logic (1245 LUTs), quantization of out-of-range states, and a hard dependency on a specific FPGA target (Gowin GW5AST-LV138) with custom RTL design. It can fail if connectivity or state precision exceeds the encoding's assumptions, if non-LIF neuron dynamics are needed, or if the design must be ported to different hardware, since the gains are tied to that device's BSRAM and LUT budget.

Order-preserving deferred expansion cuts external memory traffic by 54.5%-57.9% and peak queue data by 95.6%-96.5%; a 24-bit shared-codeword encoding reduces BSRAM usage from 438 to 270 blocks with 1245 extra LUTs, enabling the full 166.7k-neuron Drosophila CNS connectome to run in real time on one FPGA.
